guide.summary: Notion supports OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow through public connections that users can install in any workspace. You can create and use an unlisted public connection without any Notion review; a security review applies only if you want a Marketplace listing. The one decision to get right is installation scope, which cannot be changed after creation. Each user authorizes individually, refresh tokens rotate on every refresh, and the authorize URL must always carry owner=user.

reasons_to_bring_own: You want a Notion Marketplace listing, which requires your own public connection set to Any workspace and a Notion security review.

Rate limits (180 req/min, or 600 req/min on Business and Enterprise workspaces) and any API restriction Notion imposes are applied per connection, so owning the connection keeps those under your control.
build_or_borrow.verdict: Use Composio managed auth to start; you do not need your own app yet because an unlisted Notion public connection needs no review, so you can create your own later in minutes when you want a Marketplace listing or control over per-connection rate limits.

prerequisites.text: A Notion account with a workspace to use as the development workspace, which the creation form requires.
Your OAuth redirect URI(s) decided before creating the connection, since the form requires them.
A decision on installation scope (Any workspace or selected workspaces). It is permanent, and only Any workspace is eligible for the Marketplace.
Workspace owner role is required only if you create an internal connection instead. The claims do not state a role requirement for public connections.

redirect_uri_rules: At least one redirect URI must be registered on the creation form, and more than one can be registered.
Send redirect_uri in the token request if you sent it in the authorize URL or if the connection has more than one redirect URI configured. Otherwise you must not send it.
If the user cancels, Notion redirects to your redirect URI with an error query parameter such as access_denied.

blockers.text: Notion can restrict a connection's API access. This returns a 429 that must not be retried.
blockers.workaround: Treat that 429 as terminal for the connection: stop retrying and alert yourself. Separately back off on ordinary rate limiting, which is 180 req/min, or 600 req/min on Business and Enterprise workspaces.

blockers.text: There is no documented workspace-admin-wide approval. Every user must authorize individually, and only that user can share pages with the connection.
blockers.workaround: Design onboarding so each user goes through the OAuth flow themselves and picks the pages to share. Do not assume one admin install covers a team.

blockers.text: Users can cancel at the consent step.
blockers.workaround: Handle the error=access_denied query parameter on your redirect URI and offer a retry.

app_specific_gotchas.text: Installation scope (Any workspace or selected workspaces) cannot be changed after creation. If you pick selected workspaces and later want a Marketplace listing, you must create a new connection.
The owner parameter in the authorize URL must always be set to user.
Refreshing a token returns a new refresh token as well, so you must persist the rotated refresh token every time.
The token request uses HTTP Basic auth with client ID and secret. The redirect_uri field is required in some cases and not allowed in others.
There is no OAuth discovery document on notion.so, so hardcode the authorize and token endpoints.

steps.title: Draft the connection details
steps.detail_md:
Prepare what the creation form asks for: a connection name, the development workspace you will use, the redirect URI(s) for your OAuth callback, and the capabilities (read, update, insert content, etc.) your agent actually needs. Ask for the narrowest capabilities that work. You can register more than one redirect URI (for example local dev and production). Note that with multiple URIs, `redirect_uri` becomes mandatory in the token request.

Alternative: Composio lists a managed-auth Notion toolkit. If you use that, you may not need your own connection. The rest of this guide assumes you register your own.

steps.title: Decide installation scope (irreversible)
steps.detail_md:
The form makes you choose **Any workspace** or **Selected workspaces only**. This cannot be changed after creation.

- **Any workspace**: users in any Notion workspace can install it, and it is eligible for a Marketplace listing later.
- **Selected workspaces**: locked to those workspaces. If you later want a Marketplace listing, you must create a new connection.

For an agent other people will connect, pick Any workspace unless you have a specific reason not to. This is your call; the agent can only lay out the trade-off.

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail_md:
Log in to the Notion Developer portal connections page (`https://app.notion.com/developers/connections`, confirmed reachable). In the sidebar, under **Build**, choose **Public connections**, then **Create new connection**. Fill in name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities from steps 1 and 2.

Note: creating an *internal* connection requires workspace owner role. Whether that role is needed for a public connection is not stated in the claims.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail_md: Open the new connection's **Configuration** tab and copy the OAuth client ID and client secret into your secret store. Do not commit them.

steps.title: Build the authorization redirect
steps.detail_md:
Send users to `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize` using the authorization code flow with `response_type=code`, your client ID, your redirect URI, and `owner=user` (always required). Handle the cancel case: Notion redirects back with an `error` query parameter such as `access_denied`. Show a clear retry path instead of a stack trace.

There is no OAuth/OIDC discovery document on notion.so, so hardcode the endpoints.

steps.title: Implement the code exchange
steps.detail_md: POST the code to `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token` using HTTP Basic auth with client ID and secret. Include `redirect_uri` only if you sent it in the authorization URL or if the connection has more than one redirect URI. Otherwise it is not allowed. The response contains an access token and a refresh token; store both per user.

steps.title: Implement refresh with rotation
steps.detail_md: Refresh against the same token endpoint. Each refresh returns a new access token **and a new refresh token**. Persist the new refresh token atomically and discard the old one, or you will lock users out. Guard against concurrent refreshes for the same user. Access token lifetime is not documented in the claims, so refresh on 401 rather than on a guessed timer.

steps.title: Handle rate limits and restrictions
steps.detail_md: Per-connection limits: 600 req/min for Business and Enterprise workspaces, 180 req/min for all other plans. Throttle to the lower number unless you know the plan. Notion can also restrict a connection's API access with a **non-retryable 429**. Detect it, stop retrying, and surface it to the user and to you.

steps.title: Test end to end in your workspace
steps.detail_md: Run the full flow yourself: authorize, exchange, call the API, refresh, cancel. Remember each user authorizes individually, and after authorization only that user can interact with or share pages with the connection. There is no workspace-admin-wide approval described, so plan onboarding copy that tells every user to connect and share pages themselves.

steps.title: Ship as an unlisted public connection
steps.detail_md: You can release now. A Notion security review is only required for a Marketplace listing; unlisted public connections can be created and used without it. With Any workspace scope, users in any workspace can install via OAuth.

steps.title: Optional: submit a Marketplace listing
steps.detail_md: Only if you want discoverability. Listing details are managed separately in the portal's **Listings** section, require Any workspace scope, and go through Notion's security review. What the listing form requires is not covered in the claims.

steps.title: Optional: wait for Marketplace review
steps.detail_md: Notion owns this. Review duration is **not documented**; the 0 here means unknown, not zero. Your unlisted integration keeps working while you wait.

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: Yes, Notion requires a public integration to go through its review and approval process before arbitrary workspaces outside the owner's own can connect.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say a Notion security review is required only before Marketplace listing, and unlisted public connections can be created and used without it. Any workspace installation is eligible without listing.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Notion review typically takes about 5 business days to complete.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not mention review turnaround time.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: An unapproved public integration can only be installed in the workspace where it was created, with no more than 1 external workspace connection allowed.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say public integrations can be installed by users in any Notion workspace via OAuth, and unlisted connections work without review. No limit of one external connection appears in the claims.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Creating and submitting a Notion public integration is free, with no fee required.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not mention fees or pricing for creating or submitting a public connection.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: Submission requires a privacy policy URL, a company website, a demo video, and a clear description of data use, but no business verification.
belief_diff.finding: The claims list only the creation form fields (connection name, development workspace, redirect URIs, capabilities) and do not mention a privacy policy, company website, demo video, data-use description, or business verification.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS and exactly match a registered URI, with localhost HTTP permitted only for development.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say multiple redirect URIs can be registered and the redirect_uri field is required in the token request when multiple are configured. They do not address HTTPS requirements or localhost rules.
